epitaxy_or_stack: x-cut LN coupon 30 um wide x 300 nm thick printed on a 1.5 um wide x 300 nm thick SiN strip (hybrid mode)
notes: Unbalanced MZM with one printed coupon per arm, arms driven 180 degrees out of phase (p.5-6). Frequency response (Fig. 8(b)) falls to about -4.5 dB by 3 GHz then sits near -6 to -7 dB flat to 35 GHz; the authors attribute the early roll-off to probe mismatch and claim a flat response, but give no 3 dB bandwidth, so bw3db_ghz is empty. Propagation loss is from coupon cut-back structures, not the MZM; transition loss 1.8 +- 0.2 dB per facet and 16.9 dB grating-coupler/reference loss have no column. No on-chip IL for the MZM, electrode type (lumped or traveling-wave), electrode width, BOX thickness or substrate stated. Distinct from tan2024 (ring on silicon) and from the 2 mm printed LN-on-SiN MZM vanackere2023, cited here as Vpi 14.8 V. The 1550 nm wavelength is stated for the loss and ER measurements; the wavelength of the 100 Hz Vpi measurement is given only as the quadrature point.

il_onchip_excludes: grating couplers and straight-waveguide loss (normalised out against a 500 nm straight waveguide with an LN coupon)
epitaxy_or_stack: 220 nm SOI racetrack (370 nm wide, R = 15 um, 400 um straights) under a 600 nm x-cut TFLN coupon, 1 um SiO2 cladding
notes: Resonant device: no Vpi voltage; vpil is the simulated phase-shifter VpiL (per hybrid waveguide, E field in the same direction in both straights). Tuning 3.89 pm/V measured at about 1566 nm vs 3.81 pm/V simulated at 1550 nm. Ring: straights 400 um each, bend radius 15 um, phase-shifter coverage f = 0.894 (p.3-4); total phase-shifter length 0.8 mm is derived. ER 20-37 dB across resonances. Journal version of record (ACS Photonics 11, 1920) not read. Shares the Ghent/imec micro-transfer-printing line with niels2025a (different device: ring on SOI vs MZM on SiN, 600 nm vs 300 nm LN) and vanackere2023. No electrode type or drive stated. ER 37 dB is the best resonance in the transmission spectrum (Fig. 6(a), dips about 37-39 dB near 1548-1550 nm); the 1566 nm resonance used for tuning and Q is shallower in Fig. 6(a), so ER and wavelength come from different resonances. Eye open at 45 Gbit/s; BER about 2e-4 at 44-45 Gbit/s (Fig. 8(b)), above the 1e-4 bound the text gives up to 40 Gbit/s.
